did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Babylonian siege of Jerusalem began in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the tenth month, when Nebuchadnezzar arrived with his entire army and surrounded the city.
Did you know? Jerusalem was breached only in the eleventh year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month—after a prolonged siege.

Did you know? After the city was breached, the officials of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the Middle Gate. The chapter names among them Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsekim, and Nergal-sharezer.
Did you know? When Zedekiah saw the officials of Babylon, he and the soldiers fled from Jerusalem by night through the king’s garden, by the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.

Did you know? The Chaldean army pursued Zedekiah and caught him in the plains of Jericho. From there, they brought him to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
Did you know? At Riblah, the king of Babylon executed Zedekiah’s sons and all the nobles of Judah before Zedekiah’s own eyes.
Did you know? After he saw his sons being killed, Zedekiah’s eyes were put out. He was bound in bronze chains and taken to Babylon.
Did you know? When Jerusalem was conquered, the Chaldeans burned down the royal palace and the houses of the people, and they demolished the walls of Jerusalem.
Did you know? Not all the people of Judah were exiled: Nebuzaradan left in the land the poorest people, who owned nothing, and gave them vineyards and fields.
Did you know? Although Jeremiah was regarded as Judah’s prophet, Nebuchadnezzar explicitly ordered that he be protected, not harmed, and treated according to whatever he requested.
Did you know? Jeremiah was brought out of the courtyard of the guard and handed over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan. Afterward, he lived among the people.

Did you know? Ebed-melech the Cushite was promised that he would be spared the disaster because he trusted in the Lord. He was told that his life would be spared and that he would not fall by the sword.
